title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 88
paragraphs: After they had come to agreement on these terms, Attaginos escaped out of the city; and when his sons were delivered up to Pausanias, he released them from the charge, saying that the sons had no share in the guilt of taking the Medes' side. As for the other men the Thebans handed over, they supposed they would get a trial and relied on being able to ward off the danger by payment of money; but Pausanias, when he had received them, suspecting this very thing, first dismissed the whole army of allies, then took the men to Corinth and put them to death there. These were the things that happened at Plataea and at Thebes.
